headline: Google expands Deep Review to contracts and filings
dek: The tool that vetted research papers now checks Google Docs files, the company says.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Review beyond academia
body: Google publicly launched Deep Review, an AI system that checks logical consistency and claims in complex documents (Google Research).
According to the company, it now covers Google Docs and presentations, including contracts and financial material.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the review works
s3.body: According to Google Research, the system runs in stages to:

points.t: Check claims against evidence, Google says.
Compare the text with existing work, the company says.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The verification bottleneck
body: Google says human capacity to review did not grow as fast as AI-generated content.
The company cites more than 74,000 submissions to three top AI conferences this year, versus about 45,000 in 2025 (Google Research).

stat.cap: submissions to three conferences, Google says

items.t: The company did not share the tool's price.
It did not say if access varies by document type.
Higher-level judgments stay with people, Google says.

caption.hook: Google expanded Deep Review, which vetted research papers, to contracts and Google Docs files.
body: According to Google Research, Deep Review checks logical consistency and claims in complex documents, and now covers Google Docs, presentations, legal contracts and financial material. It grew out of a pilot with four computer science conferences.

Google frames the launch as a response to a verification bottleneck, citing more than 74,000 submissions to three top AI conferences this year. Higher-level judgments stay with humans. Google did not share the tool's price.
